title: Irkutsk Plague Watch
eyebrow: Outbreak watch · nexus Irkutsk Oblast, Russia
levels: Suspected case, contacts traced, no secondary cases
Cases elsewhere in Russia or at a transport hub
summary: One death on 2 October of a 28-year-old technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, widely reported as suspected pneumonic plague. Rospotrebnadzor still says pneumonia of unknown etiology; WHO is verifying the lab results and rates public risk as low. About 200 contacts remain in the Shelekhov hospital inpatient wing, all testing negative; the governor hopes to discharge them next week. No secondary cases reported by any source as of the morning of 6 October. ECDC and the European Commission are monitoring. Four Central Asian countries have tightened border health checks; no Mongolian or Chinese measures found.

assessment: Global spread risk remains low. There is one case, no secondary transmission reported by any source after four days, and the ~200 contacts are held in one hospital wing. WHO calls the risk to the general population low; ECDC notes very limited travel between Irkutsk and the EU and that person-to-person spread of plague is usually inefficient.

The main uncertainty is information quality, not epidemiology. Official and regional statements contradict each other, posts have been edited or deleted, and Russian state media removed earlier coverage. Claims about Irkutsk hospital quarantines are now contested in both directions. Treat 'no secondary cases' as an official claim until independent reporting confirms it.

Timing matters. Plague incubation is usually 1–7 days, and pneumonic plague is at the short end. Contacts exposed by 2 October pass the 7-day mark around 9 October. We are now at day 4 with no reported illness, which is reassuring but not yet conclusive. A clean cohort after 9 October would make onward spread from this case very unlikely.

Geographic exposure: Shelekhov sits about 15 km from Irkutsk (pop. ~620,000), about 20 km from Irkutsk International Airport, and on the Trans-Siberian railway, which carries traffic to Krasnoyarsk, Ulan-Ude, Chita and the rail crossings into Mongolia (Naushki) and China (Zabaykalsk). Any case surfacing along that corridor would be the first real signal of spread.
watchFor: Laboratory confirmation or exclusion of Yersinia pestis by Rospotrebnadzor or WHO (WHO says it is verifying the results)
Any symptomatic contact, or a fever/pneumonia cluster in Shelekhov or Irkutsk
9 October: 7 days since death. Official word that all contacts remain well would make onward spread very unlikely
Discharge of the ~200 contacts from Shelekhov hospital (governor: hoped for next week)
Release of the 60+ institute staff reportedly confined inside the building
Quarantines or screening at Irkutsk airport, Irkutsk station, Ulan-Ude or Krasnoyarsk
Mongolian or Chinese action at the Naushki–Sükhbaatar or Zabaykalsk–Manzhouli crossings (none found so far)
Whether the institute's 21–22 Oct international plague conference in Irkutsk goes ahead (delegates invited from 10 capitals incl. Beijing and Ulaanbaatar)

timeline.text: Technician admitted to Shelekhov district hospital with severe pneumonia; later put on a ventilator.
Shelekhov hospital closed to admissions and discharges; district head Maxim Modin confirms the restriction.
Patient dies overnight 1–2 Oct. Rospotrebnadzor head Anna Popova flies to Irkutsk; Governor Kobzev convenes an emergency commission over a 'particularly dangerous infection'.
About 200 contacts placed under observation (Izvestia: 197).
Head of Buryatia says the woman died of plague and never visited his republic; later edits the post to say 'possibly'.
Irkutsk Aluminium Plant in Shelekhov orders masks, then edits the plague reference out of its notice. Baikalsk officials post, then delete, a travel warning about Shelekhov.
Rospotrebnadzor: cause was pneumonia of unknown etiology, no lab accident found, no plague among contacts (2 COVID-19, 2 rhinovirus).
Independent outlet Lyudi Baikala reports three-week quarantines at several Irkutsk hospitals and doctors privately calling it plague.
White House says it is monitoring and assessing options.
Local Telegram channel 'Irkutsk Political' says the Irkutsk hospitals named in quarantine reports are working normally, contradicting Lyudi Baikala.
Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan tighten sanitary controls at borders. Not border closures.
WHO: cause not confirmed, testing under way, contacts symptom-free, risk to general public low; support offered.
Kremlin tells public to rely on Rospotrebnadzor. Governor says quarantined relatives may be released next week. US State Dept urges Russia to share information openly.
RFE/RL quotes a relative saying more than 60 institute staff have been confined inside the building since 2 Oct, sleeping on floors and chairs.
Mongolia's National Center for Zoonotic Diseases relays Russia's finding that no plague was detected; no new Mongolian measures announced.
President Trump says the US will help Russia 'as much as we can' and that he has not spoken to Putin about it. Secretary Rubio says the US is monitoring but sees no cause for alarm.
Governor Kobzev says the ~200 contacts are held in Shelekhov hospital's inpatient wing, all test negative, and he hopes to discharge them next week; calls the situation unpleasant but under control.
Pro-government fact-check site Lapsha Media calls the Irkutsk hospital-quarantine reports fake, citing hospitals that say they operate normally.
European Commission says it is following the situation very closely and is ready to coordinate an EU response if needed.
Reports note the institute is still preparing an international plague-control conference in Irkutsk on 21–22 Oct, with delegates invited from 10 capitals including Beijing and Ulaanbaatar.

WHO spokesperson: WHO is verifying the event, circumstances and lab results with Russia; contacts symptom-free; general-population risk appears low. ECDC says it is monitoring and that the EU risk is limited by low travel volume.

claims.claim: Cause of death was pneumonic plague
claims.note: Media and the Buryatia head said plague; Rospotrebnadzor says unknown-cause pneumonia with no work-related pathogen found. WHO says unconfirmed. One regional site (Baikal24) wrote that regional authorities confirmed pneumonic plague; no official text found to support that.

claims.claim: Infection came from a broken test tube in the lab
claims.note: Widely reported; the institute's commission and Rospotrebnadzor say no accident occurred.

claims.claim: She fell ill after a field trip to Buryatia
claims.note: Reported via Telegram channel Mash; Buryatia's head denies she visited.

claims.claim: She returned from Thailand before falling ill
claims.note: One account cited by Meduza; no corroboration found.

claims.claim: Four or more Irkutsk hospitals under 3-week quarantine
claims.note: Lyudi Baikala sources; only Shelekhov is officially confirmed. A local Telegram channel and the pro-government fact-check site Lapsha Media say the named hospitals operate normally. No independent confirmation either way.

claims.claim: Neighboring countries closed borders with Russia
claims.note: One outlet reported closures. Official statements from KZ, KG, UZ, TJ describe heightened screening only.

claims.claim: 60+ institute staff sealed inside the institute
claims.note: Now reported by RFE/RL and Radio Svoboda citing a relative; no official comment.

claims.claim: Criminal case opened over safety violations
claims.note: Single report (Vesty.co.il); no Russian official confirmation found.
Lyudi Baikala, relayed by several outlets.

claims.claim: Official diagnosis is 'pulmonary alveolitis' of unknown cause
claims.note: Wording in Mongolia's NCZD summary of Russian findings; not seen in Rospotrebnadzor's own statements.

claims.claim: Rubio warned the plague 'could quickly spread'
claims.note: Headline framing. His remark was conditional: travel is very limited, but such an outbreak could spread if it got out. He also said there was no cause for alarm.

regions.name: Tuva / Altai

regions.name: Mongolia
regions.note: NCZD relayed Russia's no-plague finding on 5 Oct; no new border measures announced. Earlier reports of heightened alert unconfirmed. Khövsgöl natural focus active since August.

regions.name: Kazakhstan
regions.note: Health Ministry monitoring Irkutsk; preventive measures at border crossings; preliminary risk to Kazakhstan assessed as low.

regions.name: Kyrgyzstan
regions.note: All sanitary-quarantine checkpoints on heightened alert.

regions.name: Uzbekistan
regions.note: Measures to prevent import of dangerous infections.

regions.name: United States
regions.note: Trump offered help; Rubio says monitor, no cause for alarm, though spread is possible if an outbreak escaped. White House and State Dept monitoring with CDC.

regions.name: European Union
regions.note: ECDC monitoring; Commission ready to coordinate. Risk to EU judged limited by low travel volume.

Morning sweep. No new cases; level unchanged at L1. Governor: ~200 contacts held in Shelekhov hospital, all negative, discharge hoped next week. WHO verifying lab results; ECDC and European Commission monitoring (EU row added). Irkutsk hospital-quarantine claim moved to disputed after pro-government fact-check.
